lessons.title: Story Time: The Lady with the Lamp
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss the significance of a historical figure's actions.
success_criteria: I can say what Florence Nightingale did.
I can say why it was important.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what a nurse does today.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a biography extract about Florence Nightingale, modelling discussion of significance.
lessons.independent_task: Children discuss and record why Florence Nightingale's actions mattered.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension of significance — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family about Florence Nightingale.

lessons.title: Telling Time to the Quarter Hour
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to tell the time to the quarter hour.
success_criteria: I can read quarter past times.
I can read quarter to times.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap o'clock and half past from Year 1.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce quarter past and quarter to using a demonstration clock.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise reading and setting quarter past/to times.
key_questions: What time does this clock show?
Can you show me quarter to 3?

differentiation.greater_depth: Mix quarter past and quarter to confidently

lessons.assessment_notes: Record introduction of quarter hour time-telling, a new Year 2 skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Practise telling quarter past/to on a clock at home.

lessons.title: Who Was Florence Nightingale?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall key facts about Florence Nightingale's life.
success_criteria: I can say when Florence Nightingale lived.
I can say what she is famous for.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a picture of Florence Nightingale.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce Florence Nightingale's life and work during the Crimean War, improving hospital hygiene.
lessons.independent_task: Children record key facts about Florence Nightingale in a fact file.
key_questions: What did she improve in hospitals?

differentiation.support: Complete fact file with word bank

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of a significant historical individual — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family what you learned about Florence Nightingale.

lessons.title: Writing About Florence Nightingale
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write factual sentences about Florence Nightingale using the past tense.
success_criteria: I can write a fact about Florence Nightingale.
I can use the past tense consistently.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about Florence Nightingale from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a factual sentence about Florence Nightingale using consistent past tense.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 factual sentences about Florence Nightingale.
key_questions: Is your sentence in the past tense?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note factual writing with tense consistency — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family a fact about Florence Nightingale.

lessons.title: Hospital Timetables: Quarter Hour Application
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply quarter hour time-telling to a real-world timetable.
success_criteria: I can read a time on a timetable.
I can say what happens at that time.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap quarter hour times from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple hospital-themed timetable using quarter hour times.
lessons.independent_task: Children read and answer questions about a quarter-hour timetable.
key_questions: What time is the next event?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of quarter hour time-telling to a real context — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Look at a timetable together, reading quarter hour times.

lessons.title: Hospitals Then and Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare hospitals in Florence Nightingale's time to today.
success_criteria: I can describe a hospital in the past.
I can compare it to a hospital today.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what hospitals are like today.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss hospital conditions before and after Florence Nightingale's reforms, comparing to today.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a comparison chart for hospitals then and now.
key_questions: What was different about hospitals then?

differentiation.support: Complete with adult support, one difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comparison skill linked to a significant individual's impact — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Share comparisons made with the class.
lessons.home_link: Talk about a time you or a family member visited hospital.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Nightingale-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read words related to nursing and hospitals.
success_criteria: I can read nursing words.
I can read a sentence about hospitals.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to nursing-themed words (e.g. 'nurse', 'clean', 'help').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading nursing words over the week.

lessons.title: Adding and Subtracting Multiples of 10
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to add and subtract multiples of 10 to/from a two-digit number.
success_criteria: I can add a multiple of 10.
I can subtract a multiple of 10.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model adding/subtracting multiples of 10 using a 100 square, noticing the pattern.
lessons.independent_task: Children solve addition/subtraction problems involving multiples of 10.
key_questions: What happens to the ones digit?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record understanding of adding/subtracting multiples of 10 — evidence for MATHS.N2.

lessons.title: How Do We Know About Florence Nightingale?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify sources of evidence about a historical figure.
success_criteria: I can name a type of historical source.
I can say what it tells us.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss how we know things happened in the past.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce sources of evidence (photographs, letters, objects) about Florence Nightingale.
lessons.independent_task: Children look at a source about Florence Nightingale and record what it tells us.
resources_needed: Florence Nightingale source materials (photo, letter extract)
key_questions: What does this source show us?
How do we know it's true?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note early historical enquiry skill: using sources — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Look at an old photo or letter at home as a 'source'.

lessons.title: Hot-Seating Florence Nightingale
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer questions in role as Florence Nightingale.
success_criteria: I can answer a question in role.
I can use facts I've learned.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap facts about Florence Nightingale learned this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model hot-seating as Florence Nightingale, answering questions using known facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children take turns hot-seating as Florence Nightingale, answering classmates' questions.
key_questions: Florence, what was your work like?
Why did you want to help soldiers?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer unprompted, in character, with detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and factual recall in role — evidence for ENG.SL1/HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Pretend to be Florence Nightingale and tell your family about your 'work'.

lessons.title: Comparing Durations of Time
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare and sequence durations of time.
success_criteria: I can say which activity takes longer.
I can sequence activities by duration.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss which takes longer: brushing teeth or having a bath.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing durations of everyday activities.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare and sequence activity duration cards from shortest to longest.

differentiation.greater_depth: Sequence 4+ activities and estimate actual durations

lessons.assessment_notes: Record duration comparison, a Year 2 measurement objective — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare how long two activities take at home.

lessons.title: Why Is Florence Nightingale Remembered?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why a historical figure is still remembered today.
success_criteria: I can say why Florence Nightingale is remembered.
I can name something named after her.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss things named after famous people.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss Florence Nightingale's legacy (nursing profession, awards named after her).
lessons.independent_task: Children record why they think Florence Nightingale is still remembered today.
key_questions: Why do we still talk about her today?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed reasoning about her lasting impact

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of historical legacy and significance — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.home_link: Talk about someone your family admires and why.

lessons.title: Florence Nightingale Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about Florence Nightingale.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's learning about Florence Nightingale.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about Florence Nightingale, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why did soldiers need her help?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on Florence Nightingale facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Time and Number
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply time-telling and number skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can tell the time to the quarter hour.
I can add/subtract multiples of 10.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of quarter hour time-telling and adding/subtracting multiples of 10.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: time, number.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 8 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.MEA/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising telling the time over the weekend.

lessons.title: Florence Nightingale Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about Florence Nightingale's life and legacy.
success_criteria: I can name what Florence Nightingale did.
I can say why she is remembered.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about Florence Nightingale.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Florence Nightingale' display combining fact files, sources, and hot-seat notes from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about Florence Nightingale?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning, preparing to compare with Mary Seacole next week — evidence for HIST.1.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished Florence Nightingale display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about Florence Nightingale with your family.
